scenario.title: 聊健康飲食和生活習慣
scenario.context: 討論飲食和健康時，一直在講「一般的」東西：糖對身體不好、蔬菜很重要、早餐是最重要的一餐。英文講「泛指」時，冠詞的用法（a / the / 什麼都不加）是台灣人最頭痛的文法之一。

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.en: Are you on a diet? You've been eating salad all week.
lines.zh: 你在節食嗎？你整週都在吃沙拉。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Kind of. I'm trying to cut down on sugar. I have a real sweet tooth.
lines.zh: 算是吧。我在減糖，我超愛吃甜的。

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.en: Same. Sugar is my weakness, especially the bubble tea from that shop downstairs.
lines.zh: 我也是。糖是我的弱點，尤其是樓下那家的珍奶。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: I let myself have one cheat day a week. Saturday is dessert day.
lines.zh: 我每週給自己一天放縱日，星期六是甜點日。

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.en: That's smart. Vegetables are important, but so is happiness.
lines.zh: 聰明。蔬菜很重要，但快樂也是。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Exactly. And the problem with strict diets is that I get hangry.
lines.zh: 就是。而且嚴格節食的問題是我會餓到生氣。

lines.speaker: Amy
lines.en: Ha! Nobody wants to see a hangry designer.
lines.zh: 哈！沒人想看到一個餓到暴躁的設計師。

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.en: What did you do this weekend?

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: Honestly? I was a total couch potato. I watched a whole series.
lines.zh: 老實說？我整個當沙發馬鈴薯，追完了一整部劇。

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.en: Nothing wrong with that. Rest is important too.
lines.zh: 那也沒什麼不好，休息也很重要。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: True. But I ate an entire pizza, which probably wasn't great.
lines.zh: 也對。但我吃掉了一整個披薩，那大概不太好。

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.en: The pizza from that new place? Was it good?
lines.zh: 那家新店的披薩？好吃嗎？

patterns.en: I eat out more than I cook.

chinglish.wrong: The sugar is bad for the health.
chinglish.right: Sugar is bad for your health.
chinglish.why: 泛指一般的糖，不加 the。中文沒有冠詞，台灣人常把 the 當成「這個」隨便加。
泛指所有狗用複數、不加 the。I like the dogs 意思是「我喜歡這些（特定的）狗」。

chinglish.right: Breakfast is the most important meal.
chinglish.why: 最高級前一定要加 the。

chinglish.wrong: I want to eat a pizza and a coffee.
chinglish.right: I want some pizza and a coffee.
chinglish.why: 一片披薩不是 a pizza（整個披薩）；a coffee 則在點餐時可以。

grammar.title: 冠詞 a / the / 零冠詞
grammar.oneLiner: 泛指一般的東西：不可數名詞和複數名詞不加冠詞；特指雙方都知道的那個：用 the；第一次提到的單一可數名詞：用 a。
whenToUse: 泛指不可數：Sugar is bad for you. / Rest is important.
泛指複數：Vegetables are healthy. / I love cats.
特指（雙方都知道是哪個）：The pizza from that place was great.
第一次提到單一可數名詞：I ate a pizza. → The pizza was huge.
最高級、序數、獨一無二：the best, the first, the sun, the internet。
固定用法：have breakfast（三餐不加冠詞）、go to bed、at work、by bus。
grammar.whyWeGetItWrong: 中文沒有冠詞，「糖不好」「這個糖不好」「一顆糖」的差別靠語境。英文每個名詞都要決定冠詞，而「泛指」這種情況是最反直覺的：講「所有的糖」反而什麼都不加。台灣人常常 the 加太多（the sugar is bad），或最高級忘了加（most important）。

examples.correct: The coffee at this café is amazing.
examples.note: 特指這家店的咖啡，加 the。
泛指所有貓用複數、不加 the。

examples.correct: I had lunch with a client.
examples.incorrect: I had a lunch with a client.

examples.correct: It's the best ramen in town.

quiz.question: I really love ___.
quiz.explanation: 泛指所有狗：複數、無冠詞。

quiz.question: ___ bubble tea from that shop is the best. (特指)
What time do you usually have ___?
Breakfast is ___ most important meal of the day.

slang.meaning: 沙發馬鈴薯、整天窩在沙發看電視的人
slang.usage: 形容懶洋洋、不愛運動的人。

risk.note: 自嘲很常見；說別人時帶點調侃。

examples.en: I was a couch potato all weekend.
examples.zh: 我整個週末都窩在沙發上。

examples.en: My husband turns into a couch potato during the World Cup.
examples.zh: 世界盃期間我老公就變成沙發馬鈴薯。

slang.meaning: 放縱日（飲食控制時可以亂吃的一天）
slang.usage: 節食或健身期間，允許自己吃喜歡的東西的日子。

examples.en: Sunday is my cheat day. Fried chicken, here I come!
examples.zh: 星期天是我的放縱日，炸雞我來了！

examples.en: Every day seems to be a cheat day lately.
examples.zh: 最近好像每天都是放縱日。

risk.note: 幽默的說法，已經收進字典。

examples.en: Feed me before I get hangry.
examples.zh: 在我餓到發火前快餵我。

examples.en: Sorry I snapped at you. I was hangry.
examples.zh: 抱歉剛剛兇你，我是餓到暴躁。

slang.usage: have a sweet tooth = 很愛吃甜的。

examples.en: I have a huge sweet tooth. I can't say no to cake.
examples.zh: 我超愛甜食，沒辦法拒絕蛋糕。

examples.en: This dessert shop is perfect for anyone with a sweet tooth.
examples.zh: 這家甜點店很適合愛吃甜的人。

review.question: I cook at home ___ save money.
If I ___ (know) it had so much sugar, I wouldn't have ordered it.
I did a ___ fast last week.
review.explanation: 複習第 62 單元：複合形容詞。

review.question: I'm used to ___ breakfast. I never eat in the morning.
review.explanation: 複習第 58 單元：be used to + V-ing。

review.question: The café ___ closed. The lights are off.
review.explanation: 複習第 50 單元：推測過去。

review.question: I'd rather ___ salad than fried chicken today.
review.explanation: 複習第 34 單元：would rather + 原形。

review.question: Which is the most natural?
options: Can I get a latte, please?

options: The sugar is bad for you.
A sugar is bad for you.
